Notes pinned on a served map

Source: R/notes.R
rr_notes.Rd

A map served with rr_serve(notes = ) takes notes: in its Notes group the reader presses "Add a note", clicks the map and writes, and the server writes the note to the file, a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with a point for each note. A note keeps its id, its time (UTC), its author ("reader" from the page), its text, the map's zoom and the page's address (its query and position: the view and layers as the reader saw them), and under, the features under it: each "layer: title", from the layers whose popup has a title. A reply joins a note's thread (reply_to, the first note's id) at its place. The page shows a pin for each thread, red while its last word is the reader's and blue once answered, with the thread and a box to reply in on a click, and asks for the notes again when it regains the focus and every 30 s.

Usage

rr_notes(path)

rr_notes_add(
  path,
  text,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  author = "analyst",
  reply_to = NULL
)

Arguments

path

The notes' file (.geojson).

text

The note's text.

lon, lat

Where it is pinned. A reply's place is its thread's.

author

Who wrote it.

reply_to

The id of the note it answers; a reply to a reply joins the same thread.

Value

rr_notes(): a data frame, a row for each note in the order written: id, thread (the id of its thread's first note), reply_to, time (POSIXct, UTC), author, text, lon, lat, zoom, under (the features under it, separated by "; ") and address; no rows when there is no file. rr_notes_add(): the new note's id, invisibly.

Details

rr_notes() reads the notes, rr_notes_add() adds a note or a reply from R: a dialogue about places on a map, between a reader in the page and someone at R (or an assistant reading the file). Both may run while the map is served, in this R session or another: each write replaces the file whole, by a rename. The file is plain GeoJSON, a note a line, and opens in any GIS. Notes are written only by R in a UTF-8 locale, where letters outside ASCII are kept as they are.

See also

rr_serve()

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
rr_notes_add(f, "Is the bank's edge here?", lon = -14.6, lat = 64.0, author = "reader")
rr_notes_add(f, "Yes, at the 200 m contour.", reply_to = 1, author = "analyst")
rr_notes(f)[, c("id", "thread", "author", "text")]
#>   id thread  author                       text
#> 1  1      1  reader   Is the bank's edge here?
#> 2  2      1 analyst Yes, at the 200 m contour.
# a map served with them: rr_serve(m, notes = f)
